title: HUD Fair Market Rents and Income Limits API (HUD User)
agency: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Office of Policy Development and Research
questions: fair market rent for a two-bedroom in a county
HUD income limits for a family of four
fair market rents for every county in a state
Small Area FMRs by ZIP code in a metro

manual.how: With a HUD User token, run the download script in the bundle (the token goes in a header, so browser links do not work). Without a token, download the published files: FMRs at https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr.html and income limits at https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/il.html (choose the fiscal year and download its data file), save it as CSV, and upload it.

cache.why: Values change once a fiscal year (with occasional mid-year revisions); queries are small.

redistribution.why: FMRs and income limits are U.S. government works published by HUD (17 U.S.C. 105); the HUD User API terms govern access, not reuse of the values.

citation: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, {dataset}, HUD User FMR and Income Limits API, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which fiscal year? FMRs and income limits are set per federal fiscal year; FMRs take effect October 1 (FY2027 on October 1, 2026), income limits when HUD publishes them in spring (FY2026 on May 1, 2026), so the latest years differ. The default is the latest of each.
In a Small Area FMR metro, the metro-wide value or ZIP-code values?
